-   **Rarity note:** Common species in Florida, found in dry open areas.

## Natural history notes

A medium-sized songbird characterized by its gray upperparts, pale underparts, black mask, hooked bill, and black wings with white patches. In Florida, it is found in open habitats such as dry prairies, pastures, scrub, pine flatwoods, agricultural edges, roadsides, and utility corridors where scattered shrubs, fences, or small trees provide hunting perches. It feeds mainly on large insects, lizards, small birds, and small mammals, often hunting from exposed perches and sometimes impaling prey on thorns or barbed wire for storage.
